statusTransitions.enforcementPoint: src/integrations/compatibility/domain/status.ts evaluateCompatibility(record, inventory?) — the ONE status transition function. Status is NEVER a field on any record, registry entry or projection (DemoMirrorEntry has no status-shaped field at all — pinned by test), so the only way to obtain a status is the pure derivation over the evidence facts.
statusTransitions.rules: The five strict ACR-006 §4 admission rules are evaluated explicitly and auditably (ruleResults carry per-rule satisfied + detail): EVERY_DECLARED_EDGE_DELEGATED (an explicitly reclassified non-AI edge with its mandatory justification is not an AI edge — ordinary domain logic never has to surrender), DIRECT_EGRESS_ABSENT_OR_BLOCKED (observed-clean, or deny-mode provably-blocked with every violation blocked — a claimed provably-blocked without blocked violations is a named inconsistency), CORPUS_FUNCTIONALLY_USABLE, ZECK_EVIDENCE_FOR_EVERY_DELEGATED_EDGE (every declared execution id correlated — found + ledger events + verification results — AND at least one execution per edge resolved terminal COMPLETED with a durable PASS, the executions authority's own completion binding), NO_FIXTURE_COUNTED_AS_EXTERNAL_PASS (every delegated edge live-basis AND recordBasis live-proof — a fixture record can never certify, regardless of contents).
statusTransitions.coverageGate: The work order's omitted-edge invariant is a sixth gate beside the five rules: a hard static no-bypass coverage defect (UNDECLARED_EDGE or INVENTORY_MISSING) alone forbids AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE even when all five rules pass over the declared graph.
statusTransitions.precedence: BYPASS_DETECTED (any direct-provider disposition or observed-passing egress violation) overrides everything; then AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE (five rules + no hard coverage defect); then BLOCKED (no progress AND every undelegated edge not-run with an external owner — provider/operator); then PARTIAL (progress exists, admission unmet); else UNASSESSED.
statusTransitions.demonstratedIn: tests/unit/compatibility/status-admission.test.ts (17 tests: each rule discriminates alone — a weakened rule fails here; the precedence matrix; the fixture-record clause; the synthetic positive COMPLETE case over a SYNTHETIC live-proof-shaped record, a unit proof of the admission FUNCTION, not a certification of any application) + the fixtures' honest derivations (example-coding-assistant → UNASSESSED; example-rag-knowledge-app → PARTIAL — asserted again through the demo surface's own projections in demo-no-upgrade.test.ts and the live server in demo-mirror-routes.test.ts).

noBypassFindings.staticReconciliation: src/integrations/compatibility/domain/no-bypass.ts reconcileExecutionGraph(declared, discovered): UNDECLARED_EDGE (a discovered edge absent from the declared graph — matched by edge id AND by the component::surface::externalExecution chain, so an id-renamed hidden edge cannot hide), INVENTORY_MISSING (no discovery produced — missing evidence is not evidence of absence), DECLARED_EDGE_UNDISCOVERED (informational divergence, named never silently resolved). hasHardCoverageDefect separates the hard defects from informational ones.
noBypassFindings.negativeTests: tests/unit/compatibility/no-bypass-negatives.test.ts (9 tests): (1) the hidden direct-provider edge — a record whose declared graph is otherwise FULLY satisfying (live traces, clean egress, verified corpus) cannot certify when the discovery finds an undeclared edge (the finding is named UNDECLARED_EDGE; the five rules may all pass over the DECLARED graph — the coverage gate refuses; an id-renamed hidden edge is still caught by chain matching; the egress observation corroborating the hidden edge escalates to BYPASS_DETECTED; the sanity twin proves the gate is the omission — the same record with the edge declared AND delegated certifies); (2) the missing edge inventory — a null inventory is the named INVENTORY_MISSING defect and alone forbids AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE (the record stays PARTIAL — progress exists, nothing reconciled); a missing DISPOSITION is likewise a named coverage defect (EDGE_MISSING_DISPOSITION).
noBypassFindings.runtimeEgress: The proof-environment egress harness (adapters/egress-deny-harness.ts, injected-transport, provider-neutral host patterns, fail-closed) is the runtime axis: DENY mode blocks + records (provably-blocked observation), OBSERVE mode records pass-through violations (violations-detected — a detected bypass). The egress kill test (tests/unit/compatibility/egress-harness.test.ts, 7 tests) pins: a denylisted request NEVER reaches the wrapped transport, the violation is recorded with host/rule/timestamp/redacted-URL, wildcard subdomain patterns block, non-denylisted hosts (the Zeck API endpoint) pass untouched, and the observation derives the honest status vocabulary.

forSiblings: PPR-018/PPR-019 consume ONE import surface: src/integrations/compatibility/public (the barrel). Do not create parallel compatibility types — the certification gate (the Lead's) reads YOUR evidence records through THIS layer's evaluation.

Declare your pinned application's graph with the domain types (ExecutionGraphEdge / ApplicationExecutionGraph; validateExecutionGraph fail-closed). Both revision pins are mandatory and immutable; a demo entry whose pins mismatch the bound record is a named defect, never rendered.

Record your proof as a CompatibilityEvidenceRecord (recordBasis 'live-proof'; validateCompatibilityEvidenceRecord / service.buildRecord fail closed). Dispositions are per-edge: delegated (zeckExecutionIds + evidenceBasis — only 'live' counts toward rule 5), direct-provider (a bypass — honest recording), not-run (cause + owner: provider/operator owners are the external BLOCKED routing), non-ai (mandatory auditable justification).

Wrap your proof runtime's outbound transport in createEgressDenyHarness({ mode, denyRules, fetchImpl, now }) — DENY mode for the provably-blocked proof, OBSERVE mode for bypass detection; record harness.observation() verbatim as the record's egressObservation.

Correlate through createCompatibilityService({ traceSource }) — bind createExecutionsServiceTraceSource({ service }) in-process, or implement the neutral ZeckTraceSource port over the SDK's public reads (getExecution/listEvents/listVerificationResults wire shapes — the trace-correlation test's SDK-shaped stub is the template); service.correlate(record) produces the ZeckTraceFact[] to record back into the record (durable evidence: found + ledger events + verification results, and at least one terminal COMPLETED with a PASS per edge).

Assess with service.assess(record, discoveredInventory) — the inventory is MANDATORY for certification (a null inventory is the INVENTORY_MISSING hard coverage defect); the returned CompatibilityAssessment carries the derived status, the five per-rule results and every named finding.

Register your demo by binding a DemoMirrorEntry to your record id (the entry has NO status field — the status is derived on every render; run availability activates only at AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE with a pinned-runtime runBinding). File your evidence record through the file store convention (one <recordId>.json per record — createFileCompatibilityEvidenceStore validates fail-closed) and the demo registry re-binds through the same resolution path.

Your certification gate: AI_EXECUTION_COMPLETE requires all five admission rules AND no hard coverage defect — a hidden edge, a missing inventory, a fixture basis or an unresolved execution each alone forbid it. The definition cannot be relaxed to make a demo pass: relaxation would have to edit evaluateCompatibility, whose discriminating power every rule's negative test pins.

limitations: The Demo Mirror's route/cost/usage sections render the correlated executions' OPTIONAL projected facts; the fixture demos carry none (honest 'not carried in this record' states) — the projection becomes non-null only when a real proof's executions carry the ledger facts.

The demo registry's default record source is the code-resident fixture set; real records ride the file-based store contract (the dashboard's record source extends to it when the sibling proofs land — one resolution path, no drift).

The BLOCKED-vs-PARTIAL boundary uses the documented external-owner rule (provider/operator owners on every undelegated edge with no proof progress); owner vocabulary honesty is the recording party's responsibility and the evaluation names every not-run edge's owner in its findings.

The egress harness's host patterns are proof-environment configuration (opaque strings); the harness itself imports no network runtime module and constructs no transport — real-runtime wrapping is the sibling proofs' act.
